pages.ja:
日が落ちる。
灰色の空が茜色に染まった頃、俺たちは城の広間に戻ってきた。
pages.jaRuby:
日が落ちる。
灰色の空が茜色に染まった頃、俺たちは城の広間に戻ってきた。
pages.en:
The sun sinks.

By the time the gray sky stains crimson, we are back in the castle's great hall.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The sun is setting.
We return to the hall when the sky turns red.

pages.ja:
……瓦礫の山に少女の亡骸はない。
たった今、遠坂と二人で中庭に埋葬してきた。
サーヴァントの常か、黒い巨人の亡骸は風化してしまったが、その砂だけでも少女と同じ棺に納めた。
pages.jaRuby:
……瓦礫の山に少女の亡骸はない。
たった今、遠坂と二人で中庭に埋葬してきた。
サーヴァントの常か、黒い巨人の亡骸は風化してしまったが、その砂だけでも少女と同じ棺に納めた。
pages.en:
…The girl's body is no longer lying among the rubble.

Tohsaka and I have just buried her in the courtyard.

The black giant's body had vanished, as Servants' bodies do. We gathered up what sand remained and laid it in the girl's coffin.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…The corpse of the girl is not on the mountain of rubble.
We just buried her in the courtyard.
I don’t know if it’s normal for Servants, but the black giant turned into sand. But we put the sand in the same coffin as the girl.

pages.ja:
「さて。これからどうするかだけど、考えはある？」
「……考え中だ。事態がまた悪い方に転んだからな。少し整理しないとやってられない」
pages.jaRuby:
「さて。これからどうするかだけど、考えはある？」
「……考え中だ。事態がまた悪い方に転んだからな。少し整理しないとやってられない」
pages.en:
“Now. Have you thought of what we do next?”

“…I'm still thinking. Things have taken another turn for the worse. I need a moment to put them in order.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Well. Do you have any ideas on what to do now?”
“…I’m still thinking. The situation just got worse. I can’t think unless I get this sorted out.”

pages.ja:
「そうね。……最大の敵だったイリヤスフィールとバーサーカーはいなくなったけど、代わりにワケわかんないヤツが出てきたし。
サーヴァントは七人しか呼ばれない筈なのに、あいつで八人目でしょう。……どう見ても既存のサーヴァントじゃなかったけど、慎二のヤツ、どこであんなのと契約したんだか」
pages.jaRuby:
「そうね。……最大の敵だったイリヤスフィールとバーサーカーはいなくなったけど、代わりにワケわかんないヤツが出てきたし。
サーヴァントは七人しか呼ばれない筈なのに、あいつで八人目でしょう。……どう見ても既存のサーヴァントじゃなかったけど、慎二のヤツ、どこであんなのと契約したんだか」
pages.en:
“So do I. …Illyasviel and Berserker, our greatest enemies, are gone, but now something incomprehensible has appeared in their place.

“Only seven Servants are supposed to be summoned, and he makes eight. …He obviously wasn't one of the original seven, so where did Shinji manage to contract with something like that?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Yeah. …The strongest enemy, Illyasviel and Berserker, are gone, but an unknown foe came out in their place.
There should only be seven Servants, but he makes eight, right? …He’s not a Servant that should exist. How did Shinji make a contract with such a guy?”

pages.ja:
……八人目のサーヴァント、か。
慎二の連れていたあの男は、サーヴァントと扱っていい存在とは思えない。
英霊に対して絶対的に優位な英霊。
底なしの宝具を持ち、およそ人間らしい感情を持たない悪鬼だ。
pages.jaRuby:
……八人目のサーヴァント、か。
慎二の連れていたあの男は、サーヴァントと扱っていい[ruby text=もの o2o=1]存在とは思えない。
英霊に対して絶対的に優位な英霊。
底なしの宝具を持ち、およそ人間らしい感情を持たない悪鬼だ。
pages.en:
…The eighth Servant.

The man Shinji brought with him is no mere Servant.

A Heroic Spirit with an absolute advantage over every other Heroic Spirit.

A demon with a bottomless store of Noble Phantasms and scarcely a trace of human feeling.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…An eighth Servant, huh?
I don’t think we can treat that man as a Servant.
He is a heroic spirit that dominates all others.
He has a seemingly infinite supply of Noble Phantasms, and he is a devil without any human emotion.

pages.ja:
「
ギルガメッシュ。それって古代メソポタミア神話に出てくる英雄だよな」
pages.jaRuby:
「
ギルガメッシュ。それって古代メソポタミア神話に出てくる英雄だよな」
pages.en: “—Gilgamesh. He's the hero from ancient Mesopotamian myth, isn't he?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Gilgamesh. That’s the hero appearing in a myth of ancient Mesopotamia, right?”

pages.ja: 「ええ。半神半人の英雄。ウルクの王、不老不死の探求者。この世の全てを治めたとされる暴君だけど、まさかあんなイカレたヤツだったとは思わなかったわ」
pages.jaRuby: 「ええ。半神半人の英雄。ウルクの王、不老不死の探求者。この世の全てを治めたとされる暴君だけど、まさかあんなイカレたヤツだったとは思わなかったわ」
pages.en: “Yes. A hero born of god and man. King of Uruk, seeker of immortality. The tyrant said to have ruled all the world. I never imagined he would be *that* deranged.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Yeah. He’s half-human, half-god. He is the king of Uruk, and the seeker of immortality. He is said to be the tyrant that obtained everything in this world, but I didn’t think he was that crazy.”

pages.ja:
「……バーサーカーを事も無げに倒した事といい、あいつ、本気になったセイバーより強いかもしれないわね」
遠坂の声にはキレがない。
それは、新たに現れた敵が難物だから、という訳ではなさそうだ。
pages.jaRuby:
「……バーサーカーを事も無げに倒した事といい、あいつ、本気になったセイバーより強いかもしれないわね」
遠坂の声にはキレがない。
それは、新たに現れた敵が難物だから、という訳ではなさそうだ。
pages.en:
“…He disposed of Berserker without any difficulty. He may even be stronger than Saber at her full power.”

There is no conviction in Tohsaka's voice.

It does not seem to be merely because this new enemy is so troublesome.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…He defeated Berserker so easily, so he might be stronger than Saber even if she has her true powers released.”
Tohsaka doesn’t sound as sharp.
It doesn’t seem like it’s because there’s a new enemy.

pages.ja: 「……？ どうしたんだよ遠坂。奥歯に物が挟まったような言い方だけど」
pages.jaRuby: 「……？ どうしたんだよ遠坂。奥歯に物が挟まったような言い方だけど」
pages.en: “…? What's wrong, Tohsaka? You sound as though there's something you don't want to say.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…? What’s wrong? You sound like you want to say something.”

pages.ja:
「ん……ちょっとね。あいつ、確かに強かった。あれだけの数の宝具を持ってるんだから、その力は一級品でしょ。
けど、実質はどうなのかなって。わたし、あいつとバーサーカーに、そう実力差はないと感じてたんだけど」
pages.jaRuby:
「ん……ちょっとね。あいつ、確かに強かった。あれだけの数の宝具を持ってるんだから、その力は一級品でしょ。
けど、実質はどうなのかなって。わたし、あいつとバーサーカーに、そう実力差はないと感じてたんだけど」
pages.en:
“Hm… It's nothing. He was certainly strong. Anyone with that many Noble Phantasms must be a first-rate power.

“But I wonder how strong he really is. I didn't sense all that much difference between his own ability and Berserker's.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hm… well. He was certainly strong. He has so many Noble Phantasms, so he’s powerful, right?
But I’m wondering how it really is. I felt that there wasn’t much difference between him and Berserker.”

pages.ja:
むー、と考え込んだりする。
……あれ。
もしかして遠坂、あいつの強さがどんな物なのか気づいていないのかな。
pages.jaRuby:
むー、と考え込んだりする。
……あれ。
もしかして遠坂、あいつの強さがどんな物なのか気づいていないのかな。
pages.en:
She frowns and gives the matter a long, thoughtful hum.

…Wait.

Could Tohsaka have failed to understand the nature of his strength?
pages.mirrorMoon:
She ponders.
…Huh?
Could it be that Tohsaka doesn’t know about his powers?

pages.ja:
「いや、あいつ自身はセイバーやバーサーカーと同じか、きっとそれ以下だ。
そもそも英霊の強さは召喚された土地での知名度によるんだろう。ならギルガメッシュなんて英雄、こっちじゃ知ってるヤツはそうはいないぞ」
pages.jaRuby:
「いや、あいつ自身はセイバーやバーサーカーと同じか、きっとそれ以下だ。
そもそも英霊の強さは召喚された土地での知名度によるんだろう。ならギルガメッシュなんて英雄、こっちじゃ知ってるヤツはそうはいないぞ」
pages.en:
“No, I think he himself is no stronger than Saber or Berserker. Probably weaker, in fact.

“The strength of a Heroic Spirit depends on how famous they are in the land where they're summoned, doesn't it? Not many people here have even heard of a hero called Gilgamesh.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“No, he himself is about as strong as Saber or Berserker, if not weaker.
First of all, heroic spirits are as strong as their fame in the place they’re summoned, right? There aren’t many people here that know about Gilgamesh.”

pages.ja:
「
それはそうだけど、知名度による実力の変動だってそう大きいものじゃないわ。
わたしにはどうも、あの金ピカは反則めいて見えたんだけど……」
pages.jaRuby:
「
それはそうだけど、知名度による実力の変動だってそう大きいものじゃないわ。
わたしにはどうも、あの金ピカは反則めいて見えたんだけど……」
pages.en:
“—That's true, but fame doesn't change their abilities *that* dramatically.

“But Goldie looked like a walking violation of the rules to me…”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“That’s true, but the change in power from popularity isn’t that big.
It seemed to me like that goldie had an unfair advantage…”

pages.ja:
「……？」
遠坂はおかしな呼び方をする。
まあ、それはさておき。
pages.jaRuby:
「……？」
遠坂はおかしな呼び方をする。
まあ、それはさておき。
pages.en:
“…?”

That is an odd name for him.

But setting that aside—
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…?”
Tohsaka calls him by a strange name.
Well, with that aside.

pages.ja:
「いや、だから反則だって。あいつの持ってた宝具はみんな本物だ。……いや、そうじゃなくて、きっと本物の元になった武器なんだ。
ギルガメッシュは一番古い神話の英雄で、あらゆる贅沢をつくした王様だったんだろう。なら、各地の神話の元になった原典を所有していてもおかしくない」
pages.jaRuby:
「いや、だから反則だって。あいつの持ってた宝具はみんな本物だ。……いや、そうじゃなくて、きっと本物の元になった武器なんだ。
ギルガメッシュは一番古い神話の英雄で、あらゆる贅沢をつくした王様だったんだろう。なら、各地の神話の元になった原典を所有していてもおかしくない」
pages.en:
“That's because he *does* violate the rules. Every Noble Phantasm he had was genuine. …No, that's not quite right. They must have been the weapons the genuine Noble Phantasms were modeled on.

“Gilgamesh is the hero of the oldest myth, a king who exhausted every luxury the world had to offer. It wouldn't be strange if he possessed the originals that became the source of legends in every land.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“He did. All the Noble Phantasms he has are real. …No, they are all originals of the real ones.
Gilgamesh is a hero in the oldest myth, and he was a king that indulged in every possible luxury. Then it shouldn’t be strange for him to own all the originals of the legendary weapons.”

pages.ja:
「あ
じゃあなに、あいつが出してた宝具は宝具じゃなくて、ただの武器って事……？」
pages.jaRuby:
「あ
じゃあなに、あいつが出してた宝具は宝具じゃなくて、ただの武器って事……？」
pages.en: “Ah—then what? Those things he was firing weren't Noble Phantasms themselves, but just weapons…?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Ohthen what? The Noble Phantasms he used weren’t Noble Phantasms, but just weapons…?”

pages.ja:
「だろうな。あいつの宝具自身は、きっと“蔵”なんだ。
生前にあいつが集めた財宝を収納した“蔵”こそが、あいつの宝具なんだと思う」
pages.jaRuby:
「だろうな。あいつの宝具自身は、きっと“蔵”なんだ。
生前にあいつが集めた財宝を収納した“蔵”こそが、あいつの宝具なんだと思う」
pages.en:
“Probably. His own Noble Phantasm must be the *storehouse*.

“I think the storehouse holding everything he collected in life is itself his Noble Phantasm.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I’d assume so. I bet his Noble Phantasm is his ‘treasury’.
I think his Noble Phantasm is the ‘treasury’ where he kept all the weapons he collected during his life.”

pages.ja: 「……そっか。ならバーサーカーが敵わないのも当然よね。英霊たちにはそれぞれ弱点がある。全ての宝具の原型を持つんなら、相手の弱点となる物を持ち出せばいいだけの話だもの」
pages.jaRuby: 「……そっか。ならバーサーカーが敵わないのも当然よね。英霊たちにはそれぞれ弱点がある。全ての宝具の原型を持つんなら、相手の弱点となる物を持ち出せばいいだけの話だもの」
pages.en: “…I see. Then it's only natural that Berserker couldn't defeat him. Every Heroic Spirit has a weakness. If he owns the prototypes of every Noble Phantasm, he only has to bring out whatever exploits the weakness of the hero before him.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…I see. Then it’s natural that Berserker couldn’t beat him. Every heroic spirit has a weak point. If he has the originals of every Noble Phantasm, he just needs to take out the one that is the most effective against his enemy.”

pages.ja:
……そういう事だ。
勝機があるとしたら、あいつはそれぞれの武器を全て使いこなしてはいない、という事。
セイバーやランサーのように、自己の武器を極限まで使いこなす“担い手”でないのならば、まだ勝てる方法がある気がする。
とまあ、それはともかく。
pages.jaRuby:
……そういう事だ。
勝機があるとしたら、あいつはそれぞれの武器を全て使いこなしてはいない、という事。
セイバーやランサーのように、自己の武器を極限まで使いこなす“担い手”でないのならば、まだ勝てる方法がある気がする。
とまあ、それはともかく。
pages.en:
…Exactly.

If there is any hope of victory, it lies in the fact that he has not mastered every one of those weapons completely.

If he is not the true *wielder* of any one weapon, the way Saber and Lancer have taken their own weapons to the absolute limit, then perhaps there is still a way to defeat him.

But never mind that for the moment.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…That’s right.
If there is a chance of victory, it is that he is not a master of these weapons.
He is not a “wielder” that has mastered his weapon to the limit, so I think there is still a way to beat him.
But with all that aside…

pages.ja:
「なあ遠坂。ほんっとーに関係ないんだけど、なんで金ピカなんだよ、あいつ」
「え……！？ あー、いや、それはその、髪が金色だったから、とか」
pages.jaRuby:
「なあ遠坂。ほんっとーに関係ないんだけど、なんで金ピカなんだよ、あいつ」
「え……！？ あー、いや、それはその、髪が金色だったから、とか」
pages.en:
“Hey, Tohsaka. This has absolutely nothing to do with anything, but why are you calling him Goldie?”

“What…!? Oh, well, that's because… his hair was gold, or something.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hey, Tohsaka. This has nothing to do with this, but why did you call him goldie?”
“Huh…!? Um, I guess… um, he had golden hair.”

pages.ja:
「なに言ってんだ。それならセイバーも金ピカなんて呼んでた筈だ。金ピカ。すごいぞ、実に意味ありげじゃんか。なんか、他に気付いた事があったからそう口にしたと見た」
「え
」
pages.jaRuby:
「なに言ってんだ。それならセイバーも金ピカなんて呼んでた筈だ。金ピカ。すごいぞ、実に意味ありげじゃんか。なんか、他に気付いた事があったからそう口にしたと見た」
「え
」
pages.en:
“What are you talking about? Then you'd call Saber Goldie too. *Goldie*. Come on, it sounds incredibly significant. You must have noticed something else about him and let the name slip.”

“Ah—”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“What are you saying? You should have called Saber that if that’s the case. It seemed like you said it with a lot of meaning behind it. I think you noticed something, right?”
“Huh?”

pages.ja:
「ここまできて隠すなよ。遠坂、なんか気付いたんだろ」
「ちょ、ちょっと違うってば、わたしのは士郎みたいに真面目な話じゃないから、あんまり追及しないでっ」
pages.jaRuby:
「ここまできて隠すなよ。遠坂、なんか気付いたんだろ」
「ちょ、ちょっと違うってば、わたしのは士郎みたいに真面目な話じゃないから、あんまり追及しないでっ」
pages.en:
“Don't start hiding things now. You noticed something, didn't you, Tohsaka?”

“I-it's not like that. Mine isn't a serious observation like yours, so don't make such a big deal of it!”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Don’t hide it now. You noticed something, right?”
“Y-You’re wrong. It’s nothing serious like you’re thinking, so don’t worry too much about it.”

pages.ja:
「ウソ吐け。根拠もなしで金ピカなんて呼ぶもんか。ほら、白状しろよ遠坂。今は一つでも情報が欲しいんだから」
「あ
う」
じっと遠坂を見据える。
そうして数秒。
観念したのか、遠坂ははあ、と大きく息をついた。
pages.jaRuby:
「ウソ吐け。根拠もなしで金ピカなんて呼ぶもんか。ほら、白状しろよ遠坂。今は一つでも情報が欲しいんだから」
「あ
う」
じっと遠坂を見据える。
そうして数秒。
観念したのか、遠坂ははあ、と大きく息をついた。
pages.en:
“Liar. Nobody calls a man Goldie for no reason. Come on, confess. Right now, we need every scrap of information we can get.”

“Ah—uh.”

I stare steadily at Tohsaka.

Several seconds pass.

Finally admitting defeat, she heaves a great sigh.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Don’t lie. You wouldn’t call him goldie for nothing. Come on, Tohsaka. I want as much information as possible right now.”
“UhUh.”
I stare at Tohsaka.
After a few seconds…
She sighs as if she’s given up.

pages.ja:
「……だから、それは……あいつ、高価そうなのいっぱい持ってたでしょ？ それで、ものすごくお金持ちなんだろーなー、って。
……だから金ピカ。あの金ピカ、すっごい贅沢してそうじゃない」
pages.jaRuby:
「……だから、それは……あいつ、高価そうなのいっぱい持ってたでしょ？ それで、ものすごくお金持ちなんだろーなー、って。
……だから金ピカ。あの金ピカ、すっごい贅沢してそうじゃない」
pages.en:
“…I told you, it was only… He had so many things that looked expensive, right? And I thought he must be incredibly rich.

“…So: Goldie. I mean, just look at him. He must live in outrageous luxury.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Well… he had many valuable looking things, right? So I just thought he’s really rich.
…That’s why I called him goldie. He looks like he’s living a luxurious life, right?”

pages.ja:
あはは、なんて明後日の方角を見ながら頬を掻く。
……恐ろしい。
遠坂の中では、お金持ちはみんな金ピカと評されるらしい。
そして更に恐ろしいのは、遠坂は“お金持ちっぽい”という嗅覚だけで、あのサーヴァントの本質を察していたコトだろう。
pages.jaRuby:
あはは、なんて明後日の方角を見ながら頬を掻く。
……恐ろしい。
遠坂の中では、お金持ちはみんな金ピカと評されるらしい。
そして更に恐ろしいのは、遠坂は“お金持ちっぽい”という嗅覚だけで、あのサーヴァントの本質を察していたコトだろう。
pages.en:
She scratches her cheek and laughs while staring determinedly into the distance.

…Terrifying.

Apparently, everyone with money earns the name “Goldie” in Tohsaka's mind.

More terrifying still, her nose for anyone who *looks rich* led her straight to the essential nature of that Servant.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Tohsaka scratches her cheek while looking away.
How scary.
It seems anyone who’s rich is called goldie by Tohsaka.
What’s more scary is that Tohsaka figured out the Servant’s true nature just because he “seemed rich”.

pages.ja:
「
ともあれ、厄介なヤツが出てきたものね。八人目のサーヴァントって時点で破綻してるのに、そいつ自身がジョーカーなんだもの。
……問いつめようにも監督役の綺礼は行方知れずだし。
まあ、今はキャスターの方が大事だから後回しにするしかないんだけど」
pages.jaRuby:
「
ともあれ、厄介なヤツが出てきたものね。八人目のサーヴァントって時点で破綻してるのに、そいつ自身がジョーカーなんだもの。
……問いつめようにも監督役の綺礼は行方知れずだし。
まあ、今はキャスターの方が大事だから後回しにするしかないんだけど」
pages.en:
“—In any case, another serious problem has appeared. The existence of an eighth Servant already breaks the rules, and this one is a wild card in his own right.

“…And Kirei, the overseer we'd ordinarily interrogate about it, has disappeared.

“Still, Caster matters more right now. We'll have to leave him for later.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Anyways, that’s another troublesome guy. There’s not supposed to be an eighth Servant, so he would be the Joker.
…I want to question Kirei as the supervisor, but I don’t know his whereabouts.
Well, we have to postpone that since Caster is more important right now.”

pages.ja:
……そうだった。
こうしている間にもキャスターは力を蓄えている。
キャスターの支配に抗っているセイバーも、これ以上は逆らえないだろう。
いや。
最悪の場合、セイバーさえ敵に回っている可能性だってある。
pages.jaRuby:
……そうだった。
こうしている間にもキャスターは力を蓄えている。
キャスターの支配に抗っているセイバーも、これ以上は逆らえないだろう。
いや。
最悪の場合、セイバーさえ敵に回っている可能性だってある。
pages.en:
…Right.

Caster continues to gather strength while we sit here.

Even Saber, who is resisting Caster's control, cannot defy her much longer.

No.

In the worst case, Saber may already have become our enemy.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…That’s right.
Caster is obtaining more power as we speak.
Saber should not be able to oppose Caster’s control much longer.
No.
In the worst case, Saber could already be under her control.

“—Right.

“We couldn't secure Illyasviel's cooperation, but that doesn't mean we can leave Caster alone. We'll have to find some way for the two of us to defeat her.”

“…Yes. I don't have the faintest idea how, but we have to try.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Yeah.
We couldn’t get Illyasviel’s help, but that doesn’t mean we can let them be. We’ll just have to think of a way to beat Caster with the two of us.”
“…Yeah. We don’t have any ideas, but we’ll have to.”

はあ、と溜息をついて瓦礫に腰を下ろす遠坂。

pages.en:
With a sigh, Tohsaka sits upon a heap of rubble.

“…Whew. Never thought I'd end up holding a council of war in a castle.”

I sit down beside her.
pages.mirrorMoon:
She sighs and sits on the rubble.
“…Phew. I never thought we’d have a strategic meeting in a castle.”
I follow Tohsaka’s lead and sit down.

……まあ、ここなら夜になっても暖はとれるし。
もしかすれば、イリヤスフィールが持っていた魔術品も発見できるかもしれない。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
…At least we can keep warm here after nightfall.

And we may even discover some mystic tool Illyasviel left behind.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…Well, we’ll have a bed to sleep in here.
If we’re lucky, we might even find some magical item of Illyasviel’s.

pages.ja:
そうして、二人して気を緩めた瞬間。
「止めとけ止めとけ。オマエたち二人だけで裏をかく？

呆れかえった声が、正面玄関から響いてきた。

呆れかえった声が、正面玄関から響いてきた。
pages.en:
And then, just as both of us relax—

“Give it up. The two of you think you'll outmaneuver them on your own?

“That'll never work, you fools.”

An exasperated voice rings from the main entrance.
pages.mirrorMoon:
And the moment we let our guard down…
“Get real. You’re going to defeat them just by yourselves?
That’s impossible, you idiots.”
A stunned voice comes from the front entrance.

pages.ja:
「！？」
すぐさま立ち上がって正門に振り向く。
pages.jaRuby:
「！？」
すぐさま立ち上がって正門に振り向く。
pages.en:
“!?”

We spring to our feet and turn toward the door.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“!?”
We jump up and turn to face the speaker.

pages.ja:
「いつぞやの夜以来だな、お二人さん。お互いしぶとく生き残っているようで何よりだ」
「ラ
ランサー……！？」
pages.jaRuby:
「いつぞやの夜以来だな、お二人さん。お互いしぶとく生き残っているようで何よりだ」
「ラ
ランサー……！？」
pages.en:
“Haven't seen you two since that night. Glad to see you're both still too stubborn to die.”

“L—Lancer…!?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Since that night, huh? It’s great you two are still hanging in there.”
“LLancer…!?”

pages.ja:
神経を一気に束ね、魔術回路を繋いでいく。
現れた男は紛れもなくランサーだった。

！

pages.en:
In a single instant, I draw my nerves together and connect my Magic Circuits.

The man before us is unmistakably Lancer.

…Ten nights ago, he drove that spear through my chest.

I cannot allow it to happen again.

I have to get Tohsaka away before he can swing his spear—!
pages.mirrorMoon:
I quickly concentrate and connect my Magic Circuit.
He is certainly Lancer.
…He speared my heart on that night ten days ago.
I can’t let it happen again.
I have to let Tohsaka escape before he attacks!

pages.ja:
「士郎、離れて……！ アイツはわたしが引きつけるから、その間にアンタは二階に……！」

！」

！」
pages.en:
“Shirou, get back…! I'll keep him occupied. You go upstairs while I—!”

“Run, Tohsaka…! I'll hold him here. You get outside—!”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Get away, Shirou…! I’ll keep him busy, so you run to the second floor…!”
“Run, Tohsaka…! I’ll hold him back, so you run outside!”

pages.ja:
「

pages.en:
“—Wait just a minute.

“You didn't hear a single word I said about valuing your own life, did you?”

Tohsaka immediately lowers the left hand she had aimed at Lancer—then turns it on the end of *my* nose instead.

But threat or no threat, I have complaints of my own.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hold on.
It seems you weren’t listening to me at all when I told you to value your life.”
She lowers the hand she pointed at Lancer and points at me.
But I have objections as well!

pages.ja:

「そんなワケないじゃないっ！ 相手は歩兵よ、飛び道具がない相手に飛び道具であるわたしが逃げてどうすんのよ！」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“Don't be ridiculous. I told you quite clearly I wasn't going to take your advice. Close combat is my job. I've faced him once already, so I'm better suited to this than you are.”

“Of course you aren't! He's a close-range fighter with no projectile weapon. Why should *I*, the one with ranged attacks, be the one to run!?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Don’t be stupid. I told you I won’t heed your warning. It’s my role to fight hand-to-hand. This is the second time I’m fighting him, and I’m more suited for it.”
“That can’t be true! He’s a foot soldier. How can I, the ranged attacker, run away from an enemy with no ranged weapons!?”

pages.ja: 「だからこそだろ！ 懐に入られたらおしまいって判らないか！？ いいから、遠坂は遠くから援護してくれればいいんだよ！」
pages.jaRuby: 「だからこそだろ！ 懐に入られたらおしまいって判らないか！？ いいから、遠坂は遠くから援護してくれればいいんだよ！」
pages.en: “That's exactly why! Don't you understand that you're finished if he closes the distance!? Just stay back and support me from range!”
pages.mirrorMoon: “That’s why! Can’t you tell you’ll die if he closes in on you!? You can just back me up from a distance!”

pages.ja: 「ばかっ、援護なんてできるかっ！ あいにくそんな器用な魔術なんて知らないわよ。やるならアンタごと吹っ飛ばすに決まってんじゃない！」

pages.mirrorMoon: “You idiot! I can’t back you up! I don’t know any magic that’s that precise! I bet I’ll blow you away along with him!”

pages.mirrorMoon:
“! Don’t come out with your destructive personality!

“What!?”

pages.en:
…For the next several minutes, we argue while each tries to shove the other out of the way.

By the time I am thoroughly exhausted and wondering how matters came to this, I suddenly remember—

Lancer is still at the castle entrance, watching us with an enormous grin.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…And we argue for a few minutes.
When we begin to tire and wonder how this got started…
I notice that Lancer is watching us with a smile.

“—What, finished already? I'm in no hurry. Go ahead and settle it properly. Better to get every last grievance off your chest.”

“——”

“——”

We clear our throats, chastened, and glare at Lancer.

I step half a pace forward. Tohsaka moves slightly behind me.

…Honestly, none of that would have happened if we had stood like this from the beginning.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Oh, you’re done? I’m in no hurry, so finish it off. It’s good to let out everything you have.”
“”
“”
I cough and glare back at Lancer.
I take half a step forward, and Tohsaka is right behind me.
…Man, we should have done so from the start.

pages.jaRuby: 「ああ、待て待て。せっかく同意を得たところ悪いが、こっちに戦う気はない。見るに見かねてな。少しばかり手助けしてやろう、とでしゃばりにきたワケだ」
pages.en: “Easy, easy. Sorry to interrupt just when you've finally agreed, but I'm not here for a fight. I couldn't stand by and watch any longer, so I came to stick my nose in and lend you a hand.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Oh, hold on. I’m sorry to say this after you’ve reached a compromise, but I don’t intend to fight. I was just unable to ignore you guys. I’m butting in so that I can help you guys a bit.”

pages.ja:
「な
に？」
ちょっと待て。
あいつ、今なんて言った
！？

「な
に？」

！？
pages.en:
“What—?”

Wait.

What did he just say—!?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“What?”
Hold on.
What did he just say!?

pages.ja: 「……聞き違いかしら。今、手助けをするって聞こえたけど」
pages.jaRuby: 「……聞き違いかしら。今、手助けをするって聞こえたけど」
pages.en: “…Perhaps I misheard you. It sounded as though you said you would help us.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…Did I mishear you? I think I heard that you’re helping us.”

」

」

pages.en:
“Was that difficult to understand? Then I'll say it again. The two of you can't stand against Caster and her lot. That's why I said I'd lend you my strength.”

“——”

I stare blankly.

Beside me, Tohsaka grasps the situation first.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Oh, is it hard to understand my point? I guess I’ll rephrase it. You two are no match for Caster. So I will lend you guys a hand.”
“”
I’m stunned.
But Tohsaka quickly grasps the situation.

pages.ja: 「そう。ホントにでしゃばりね、ランサー。訊くけど、それは貴方のアイデア？」
pages.jaRuby: 「そう。ホントにでしゃばりね、ランサー。訊くけど、それは貴方のアイデア？」
pages.en: “I see. You really are sticking your nose in, Lancer. Let me ask you—was this your idea?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “I see. You really are butting in. Is that really your idea?”

pages.ja: 「いや、オレのマスターからの指示だ。キャスター達がああなっちまった以上、一人きりの身としては協力者がほしいんだと。ま、連中を潰すまでの共同戦線ってヤツだな」
pages.jaRuby: 「いや、オレのマスターからの指示だ。キャスター達がああなっちまった以上、一人きりの身としては協力者がほしいんだと。ま、連中を潰すまでの共同戦線ってヤツだな」
pages.en: “No. My Master gave the order. Now that Caster and her people have gone this far, a man on his own needs allies. Call it a united front until we've crushed them.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “No, it’s an order from my Master. He wants to cooperate against Caster since he’s alone. Well, we’re just making a quick alliance until we defeat Caster.”

pages.ja: 「まっとうな理由ね。けど、それならわたしたちよりもっと頼りがいのあるヤツがいるでしょう」
pages.jaRuby: 「まっとうな理由ね。けど、それならわたしたちよりもっと頼りがいのあるヤツがいるでしょう」
pages.en: “A perfectly sensible reason. But in that case, there is someone much more dependable than us.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “That’s a sound reason. But I think there’s a more reliable guy to go talk to.”

pages.ja:
……それは慎二とギルガメッシュの事か。

pages.en:

Tohsaka appears to be fishing for whether Lancer knows about them—

…Is she talking about Shinji and Gilgamesh?
It seems Tohsaka is trying to figure out if Lancer knows about them

「……ふうん。正しい選択ね、ランサー。けど、それも貴方のマスターの指示ってワケ？」

pages.en:
“No. That one's no good. Couldn't stand the bastard.

“He's more than adequate in a fight, but watching my own back every second would get tiresome.”

“…I see. A wise decision, Lancer. But was that also your Master's order?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“No, they won’t do. I don’t want to ally with them.
I have no complaints about his power, but it’s too troublesome to worry about my back when I’m fighting.”
“…Oh. That’s the correct choice, Lancer. Is that an order from your Master as well?”

pages.ja:
「それも違うな。アンタらを選んだのは俺の趣味だ。一度面識がある分話が早いだろう」
あっさりと言う。
あの男の中では、アーチャーと戦った事も俺の胸を貫いた事も、面識で済まされてしまうらしい。
pages.jaRuby:
「それも違うな。アンタらを選んだのは俺の趣味だ。一度面識がある分話が早いだろう」
あっさりと言う。
あの男の中では、アーチャーと戦った事も俺の胸を貫いた事も、面識で済まされてしまうらしい。
pages.en:
“No again. Choosing you two was my own taste. We've already met once, so I knew we'd come to terms quickly.”

He says it without hesitation.

Apparently, fighting Archer and driving a spear through my chest count as no more than being acquainted in this man's mind.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“That’s wrong as well. I chose you two out of personal interest. You guys are easier to talk to since we’re acquaintances, right?”
He speaks plainly.
It seems that fighting Archer and driving his lance through my heart are the same as becoming acquaintances in his mind.

pages.ja: 「……待てランサー。俺はおまえに二度も殺されかかった。だっていうのに、おまえの言葉を信用すると思っているのか」
pages.jaRuby: 「……待てランサー。俺はおまえに二度も殺されかかった。だっていうのに、おまえの言葉を信用すると思っているのか」
pages.en: “…Wait, Lancer. You have nearly killed me twice. Do you honestly expect me to trust a word you say?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “…Hold on, Lancer. I was almost killed twice by you. And you think I’m going to believe you?”

pages.ja: 「思っているさ。オマエの参謀はさっぱりとしたいい女だからな。そんな女が手を貸すってんだから、オマエだって物好きなお人好しなんだろ？」
pages.jaRuby: 「思っているさ。オマエの参謀はさっぱりとしたいい女だからな。そんな女が手を貸すってんだから、オマエだって物好きなお人好しなんだろ？」
pages.en: “I do. Your strategist's a fine woman—straightforward and no-nonsense. If a woman like that is willing to lend you a hand, you must be one hell of a softhearted eccentric yourself, eh?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “I do believe so. Your commander-in-chief is a good frank woman. Such a good woman is helping you out, so you must be good-natured as well, right?”

pages.ja:

」
思わず眉を寄せる。

pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“Mm…”

I cannot help frowning.

…Though what bothers me most is that Tohsaka, who is supposed to be on my side, is nodding along with him.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hm”
I frown.
…I’m troubled that Tohsaka is nodding at our enemy’s words.

“That's why I decided I could work with you.

“—Mind you, I don't mean that *you* can cooperate with *me*. I mean that *I* decided you two were worth my cooperation.”

“……?”

Honestly, I cannot tell the difference.

“So that’s it. That’s why I thought we might be able to cooperate.
Oh, but let me tell you. It’s not ‘you guys’. ‘I’m’ the one who thought that you guys would make good allies.”
“……?”
I can’t understand the difference.
